title: In A Grove

speaker_display.monk: the traveling monk who met the couple the day before
speaker_display.narrator: the outside narrator who only introduces who is speaking
speaker_display.woodcutter: the woodcutter who found the body

items.speaker_state: Matter-of-factly reporting what he saw; no explicit emotion is stated.
items.scene: He reports the wound he saw on the body.
evidence: "One stab in the chest. That's what I saw,"

items.speaker_state: Matter-of-factly recounting his discovery and the signs of a struggle; no explicit emotion is stated.
items.scene: He describes finding the body in a thicket that morning and the objects and marks nearby.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds the circumstances and details of his discovery after reporting the wound.
evidence: "The broken bamboo and trampled earth showed a struggle."

items.speaker_state: No emotion or manner is stated; he neutrally reports when he saw them.
items.scene: The monk says he saw the couple the previous day at noon.
items.reaction_to_previous: It shifts from the woodcutter's discovery to what the monk witnessed the day before.

items.speaker_state: He expresses regret that he did not pay closer attention to the couple.
items.scene: The monk recalls seeing the couple and says he now wishes he had looked more closely.
items.reaction_to_previous: He expands on when he saw them, adding what he remembers and his regret about not looking closely.
evidence: "I hardly looked at them. Now I wish I had."

items.speaker_state: No emotion or manner is stated; he neutrally reports the capture.
items.scene: The constable reports catching Tajomaru by the stone bridge.
items.reaction_to_previous: It moves from the monk's recollection to the constable's report of catching the bandit.
evidence: "I caught Tajomaru, the famous bandit, by the stone bridge,"

items.speaker_state: He gives direct instructions and says the woman can explain what happened; no emotion is stated.
items.scene: The constable describes the bandit's condition and possessions, then directs others to find the woman.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds details about the capture and tells others to seek the woman after announcing he caught Tajomaru.
evidence: "He'd fallen from a horse, but he still had the dead man's bow."
"Find the woman. She'll tell you what he did."

items.speaker_state: No emotion or manner is stated; she identifies her daughter's husband.
items.scene: The old woman identifies Takehiro while the constable is asking that the woman be found.
items.reaction_to_previous: She responds to the constable's mention of finding the woman by identifying Takehiro as her daughter's husband.

items.speaker_state: She sounds concerned for her daughter and pleads for news before she is sent home.
items.scene: The old woman describes Masago and asks that she be found.
items.reaction_to_previous: She follows her identification of Takehiro with details about Masago and an urgent request to find her.

items.speaker_state: He admits to killing the man, then signals that he wants to defend himself against being called a coward.
items.scene: Tajomaru answers the account of the dead man's family and begins his own account.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows the old woman's plea for news with an admission of responsibility for the killing.
evidence: "But listen before you call me a coward!

items.speaker_state: He recounts the fight and his departure; the exclamation about the strokes conveys pride in the contest.
items.scene: Tajomaru describes the demand for a duel, the fight, and leaving after the man fell.
items.reaction_to_previous: He continues his account, explaining the fight and what he did after the man fell.
evidence: "Twenty-three strokes! No other man had lasted twenty."

items.speaker_state: She recounts approaching her husband after the bandit left; no emotion is stated in this line.
items.scene: At the temple, Masago begins describing what she did after the bandit left.
items.reaction_to_previous: She offers her account of what happened after the bandit's version of the fight and departure.
evidence: "I crawled towards my husband after the bandit left,"

items.speaker_state: She expresses regret and helplessness, questioning what she can do now.
items.scene: Masago describes trying to drown herself and asks where she can go.
items.reaction_to_previous: She continues explaining her actions after stabbing her husband, saying she later tried to drown herself.
evidence: "Afterwards, I tried to drown myself. I couldn't even do that."
How could I bear those eyes?

items.speaker_state: He reports what he heard; no emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: Takehiro's spirit speaks through the medium, recalling the bandit comforting his wife.
items.reaction_to_previous: His account follows Masago's account of trying to drown herself with a different recollection of what happened.
evidence: said Takehiro's spirit through the medium.

items.speaker_state: He describes sinking into darkness; no emotion or manner is stated.
items.scene: Takehiro's spirit recounts sinking into darkness after an unseen hand drew the dagger from his chest.
evidence: "I sank for ever into the darkness."
An unseen hand quietly drew the dagger from my chest.
